title: ‘Unlucky’ taunts, dowry demands: Dehradun teacher dies, husband, in-laws booked
content: A young teacher died by suicide following alleged dowry harassment by her husband and in-laws.  The victim faced months of physical and mental abuse after her marriage last November.  Her family filed a police complaint accusing her husband and his relatives of cruelty.  Authorities registered a dowry death case against the accused individuals and family members.  An investigation is currently underway following the tragic incident in Dehradun.

title: 'You dare to demand Modi's resignation?' Masked men assault protester in Bengaluru
content: A student was assaulted by masked individuals on two motorcycles.  The attackers questioned his demand for Prime Minister Modi's resignation.  He sustained serious leg injuries and required a plaster cast.  An FIR has been registered at Jalahalli Police Station.  Police are currently investigating the incident and no arrests have been made.

title: 34 killed as methane explosion tears through coal mine in Pakistan's Balochistan
content: A methane gas explosion in Pakistan's Balochistan province killed at least thirty-four miners. Ten miners remained trapped underground after the blast ripped through the coal mine. Rescue teams worked against time to locate and recover the remaining trapped workers. Authorities announced compensation for the families of the deceased miners. The incident highlights ongoing safety concerns within Pakistan's coal mining industry.

title: 'We don't have an MS Dhoni': Ex-England captain's blunt warning to Fleming
content: Michael Vaughan believes Stephen Fleming should start immediately as England's Test coach. Fleming will delay his Test coaching duties until the South Africa tour. Vaughan suggests this delay indicates a reduced appeal of the coaching role. Fleming's IPL success with Chennai Super Kings is noted. Vaughan questions if England has an MS Dhoni-like captain for Fleming.

title: 'Head of family PM Modi listens': Raghav Chadha hails 'historic' anti-paper leak Bill
content: Raghav Chadha spoke in Rajya Sabha supporting the anti-paper leak Bill. He stressed institutional solutions are needed to resolve the crisis. The Bill introduces stricter penalties for paper leaks and exam malpractices. Individuals face jail terms and significant fines for unfair means. Parliament approved the Public Examination Amendment Bill after Lok Sabha clearance.

title: Tim Cook's last Apple report card: $109.4 billion quarter and a '100-year flood'
content: Apple's Q3 2026 results marked Tim Cook's final earnings call as CEO, with revenue hitting a record $109.4 billion, up 16%. iPhone revenue rose 22% to $54.25 billion and Mac jumped 29% on MacBook Neo demand. Yet Apple stock fell up to 8% after weak September guidance. Cook cited a "100-year flood" on memory prices. John Ternus takes over September 1.

title: BJP's Shehzad Poonawalla drops party name from X bio, fuels exit speculation

However, his Instagram bio still lists him as a BJP Spokesperson. Poonawalla joined the BJP in December 2017 and has been a vocal supporter. title: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos' 'message' to customers on what is not going to change

Amazon is making artificial intelligence its largest investment, spending billions on infrastructure.  The company is also developing its chip business as a potential new major pillar.  These strategic investments aim to enhance customer service and drive continued expansion.

The situation escalated beyond a peaceful demonstration, endangering security personnel.

title: Meet José Flores, 119, who still walks, smiles and eats well
content: Born in 1907, Jose Flores could be recognized as the world's oldest living person. He is cared for by his family in their rural Costa Rican home. His impressive longevity is believed to result from a combination of dietary habits and lifestyle. Ongoing research aims to authenticate his age for global acknowledgment. His extraordinary story sheds light on the secrets of a long and healthy life.

title: Meta AI head has message for Google Cloud executive joining Scale AI

He replaces interim chief executive Jason Droege, who led the company after founder Alexandr Wang's departure. Wang congratulated deSouza on his new leadership role at Scale AI.

title: After made-in-India bullet train, high-speed corridors to get indigenous signal system
content: Indian Railways is developing an indigenous signalling protocol for high-speed rail called the Bharat Train Control System (BTCS). The system is being designed specifically for Indian operating conditions.

title: Car sold without disclosing prior billing to another buyer; Mercedes, dealer fined Rs 10L

The buyer learned of the discrepancy when servicing records showed an earlier registration date.  Both companies engaged in unfair trade practices by concealing this information.  The commission directed the dealer and manufacturer to pay Rs 5 lakh each.

title: Spain deploys military after thousands of Moroccan migrants cross border; 9 killed

Authorities confirmed an agreement with Morocco for the return of illegal migrants.  The reason for the surge remains unclear, with various factors suggested.  Ceuta, a Spanish enclave, is a key point for migration into Europe.

title: There’s a price tag on college life: How rent, food and other costs add up

Chopra faces strong competition from Arshad Nadeem and Keshorn Walcott. The final will be held at Scotstoun Stadium in Glasgow, Scotland. A tracking device shows Purja's location has shifted, offering a small hope for rescuers. Poor weather has so far prevented helicopters from taking off, delaying aerial search-and-rescue operations. Authorities were preparing to deploy helicopters on Friday morning if weather conditions improved.
